title: parse_duration returns wrong seconds for compound spoken numbers
detail: The regex alternation matches only the last number word before the unit, so 'twenty five minutes' -> 300 (5 min) and 'forty-five minutes' -> 300; '1 hour and a half' -> 3600. A timer silently set to the wrong length is worse than ASK. Words like thirteen/fifty/seventy are missing (-> None).
evidence: bcd3b75: parse_duration('twenty five minutes')=300, ('forty-five minutes')=300, ('1 hour and a half')=3600, ('one and a half hours')=None, ('thirteen minutes')=None. tests: test_brain3_duration_compound_numbers (3 fail).
fix: Tokenize a number phrase first (tens + units with optional hyphen, 'and a half', 11-19, 50/70/80), then multiply by unit; if any number word adjacent to the matched one is unconsumed return None (ASK).

title: parse_datetime silently returns wrong dates and times
detail: dateparser with PREFER_DATES_FROM=future reads bare numbers as months and drops times it cannot attach: reminders/events get created months off or at the current clock time with no ASK.
evidence: bcd3b75 at 2026-10-24T05:23Z: 'tomorrow at 9' -> 2026-10-25T05:23:33 (hour = now, not 9); 'at 3' -> 2027-03-24T00:00; 'friday at 3' -> 2027-03-24T00:00; 'the 5th at 10am' -> 2027-05-24T10:00; 'next friday at 3pm'/'tonight' -> None. tests: test_brain3_datetime_never_silently_wrong (3 fail).
fix: Pre-parse spoken patterns (weekday/today/tomorrow/tonight/morning + 'at H[:MM] [am|pm]', 'in N units') with a small rule parser; pass RELATIVE_BASE and PREFER_DAY_OF_MONTH; reject results >60 days out or whose hour differs from an explicit 'at H' -> ASK.

title: MLX forward passes run on the event loop, blocking receive loop
detail: engine.route()/engine.args() are synchronous MLX calls invoked directly inside the async utterance task. While they run, the server cannot read rpc_result, cancel, partial or new final utterances, nor send ui 'thinking'. A new utterance/cancel arriving mid-forward cannot preempt it, and a cold first route (cache build ~700-token prefill) stalls the socket for its full duration.
evidence: test_brain5_engine_does_not_block_event_loop: engine.route sleeping 0.5 s (stand-in for a forward pass) -> concurrent 20 ms ticker lagged 0.511 s.
fix: Run engine calls in a single-thread executor: `res = await loop.run_in_executor(self._mlx_pool, self.engine.route, text, ctx)` (one worker so MLX state stays serialized); check task cancellation after each await.

title: script_needs_confirm lets click/JS/open side effects run unconfirmed
detail: Allow-list logic only blocks keyword patterns; any script that targets Safari/Finder/System Events and contains one read verb (get/open/...) runs without CONFIRM. UI scripting `click button "Place Order"`, `perform action "AXPress"`, Safari `do JavaScript "...click()"`, `open location`, Finder `open file x.command` (executes) all pass. This also bypasses the press-label danger guard. Separately, _batch_confirmed (:396) lets one confirm cover every later dangerous press/keys in the same batch. Planner input includes web page text, so a prompt-injected page can drive these.
evidence: cbc4879, Orchestrator.script_needs_confirm: safari do JavaScript click -> False; System Events click 'Place Order' -> False; System Events perform AXPress 'Empty' -> False; Finder open file 'x.command' -> False; Safari open location -> False. reviews/brain/tests test_brain9_* (4 fail).
fix: Default-confirm: return False only if every statement matches a read-only allow-list grammar (get/count/exists of properties); add click|perform action|do JavaScript|open location|open file|open (non-folder) to _SCRIPT_BLOCK; scope _batch_confirmed to the confirmed action's ref/summary.

title: Bool 'on' regex override inverts mute for natural phrasings
detail: For every bool arg named `on` (mute, dark_mode, wifi, bluetooth) the utterance regex overrides the model. For mute, on/off words describe the sound, not the mute state: 'turn the sound back on' -> mute on=True (mutes), 'turn the sound off' -> on=False (unmutes); any stray 'on' ('unmute, I'm on a call') forces True. Wrong action presented as success.
evidence: cbc4879 _coerce_args('mute', {'on': X}, utterance=...): 'turn the sound back on' -> True, 'turn the sound off' -> False, "unmute, I'm on a call" -> True. test_brain10_mute_polarity (3 fail).
fix: Drop the override for mute (or invert: sound/audio on -> mute False; 'unmute' -> False first); for others only match on/off adjacent to the skill noun (r'\b(turn|switch)\s+(on|off)\b|\b(on|off)$'); otherwise trust the model and ASK if it disagrees.

title: Planner stops before the 5th action's expect; DONE accepted unverified
detail: plan() breaks as soon as the 5th action line is emitted, so that action's following `expect` line is never decoded and the orchestrator executes it with no verification (prompt rule 3 relies on expect). On the next turn a lone `done` is accepted when the previous batch had no failure (orchestrator.py:580-588), so DONE is effectively trusted whenever the model omitted expects; AGENTS.md says DONE is verified by the harness, never trusted.
evidence: planner.py:228-232 `if terminal or n_actions >= 5: break` right after queuing the action line; orchestrator.py:580 'done validation: alone in batch + no prior failure' with no verify rpc.
fix: After the 5th action keep decoding while the next line starts with `expect`/`#` (break on the first non-expect line); for done, require that the last batch had >=1 passed expect or run verify on the goal-derived predicate, else replan with 'done without evidence'.

title: Pending ASK captures any next utterance for 90 s
detail: After a planner `ask`, the next utterance within 90 s is always treated as the answer and appended to the old goal, even a new command ('set volume to 30') or 'never mind'; it skips System 1 entirely and replans the old task.
evidence: orchestrator.py:129-135@cbc4879: `if self._pending_task and time.time()-t<90: ... _planner_loop(goal, answer=text)` with no route check.
fix: Route the reply first; only treat it as an answer when the top route is ASK/MULTI_STEP-like or p_top < tau; clear _pending_task on cancel.

title: Speculative partial routes queue ahead of final route
detail: server.on_partial -> _speculative_route submits a full engine.route to the single FIFO MLX worker for every changed partial and never drops superseded ones. On a spec miss the final route (and any planner call) waits behind all stale partial routes. Spec key is lower+whitespace only, so a final that adds punctuation/capitalisation (Parakeet finals do) always misses. Net effect: speculation makes the common case slower, not faster.
evidence: reviews/brain/tests/test_brain_pass4.py: 6 partials + final with 80 ms fake route -> final waited 561 ms (expected <160). norm('Set the volume to thirty percent.') != norm('set the volume to thirty percent'). At ~10 partials/utterance and a 60-150 ms route this adds 0.5-1.5 s to time-to-action on a miss.
fix: Keep one in-flight spec: if a spec future is still queued (not started), cancel it before submitting (Future.cancel + worker skips cancelled); debounce partials (~150 ms); normalise with re.sub(r"[^\w\s]","",...) on both keys; on miss, also cancel queued spec before submitting the final route.

title: One confirm unlocks every dangerous action in the batch
detail: _batch_confirmed is set True by any model-authored `confirm "<summary>"` and by the first guarded press/type/keys, and then bypasses the danger guard for all remaining actions in the batch (up to 5, more with scripts per brain-11). The model writes the summary, so an injected or wrong `confirm "Open the chat?"` followed by `type #5 "..." enter` in Messages, or a confirmed delete followed by a second `press #<Send/Place order>`, executes without the user approving that action. Violates CONFIRM-for-irreversible.
evidence: orchestrator.py:325 `self._batch_confirmed = True      # no double confirm this batch` (op==confirm, summary from model); :400 `if needs and not self._batch_confirmed:`; reset only per batch at :534.
fix: Bind confirmation to the action: confirm op sets self._confirmed_next = 1 (applies only to the immediately following action) and the guard compares the confirmed action's ref/label; each further dangerous action asks again (or show one confirm listing all dangerous actions of the batch before executing any).

title: abs_level turns relative volume requests into near-zero absolute levels
detail: When System 1 routes change_volume/change_brightness, _run_skill switches to set_volume/set_brightness whenever any 'to|at <number>' appears anywhere in the utterance. That catches number ranges, times and incidental 'to', and silently sets volume to 2-3% (effectively mute). The design rule is that a wrong value is worse than ASK.
evidence: cloud/brain-3 14a3f52, called directly: abs_level('turn it up two to three notches')=3; abs_level('turn the volume down a bit at 3 pm')=3; abs_level('turn up the volume so I can listen to 2 songs')=2 (each becomes set_volume level=N). Correct cases: 'down to twenty'=20, 'at night'=None.
fix: Only match an anchored target at the end of the clause: r'\b(?:up|down)?\s*(?:to|at)\s+(?:the\s+)?(<level>)(?:\s*(?:percent|%))?\s*$'. Reject when the previous token is a number ('two to three') or the next token is am/pm/o'clock. Otherwise keep the relative skill.

title: Compound check adds serial route passes before every 'and' utterance
detail: On every final utterance, _compound runs before the speculative-route hit check (line 336 comes before 'spec_hit = False' at line 340). For any text containing 'and'/'then', it does one System 1 forward pass per clause, serially on the worker. The clauses are never speculated on partials. When the compound is rejected (the common case: 'search for salt and pepper' becomes 'search for salt' + 'pepper'), the user still pays 2-4 x route_ms before the normal path, which may already have a speculative hit ready. Speed is priority 1. Related risk: STT text has no quotes, so the quote guard never fires on spoken message bodies. 'tell Sam the demo is at 3 and then we eat' splits into a truncated message plus a second skill if both clauses clear 0.75.
evidence: cloud/brain-3 14a3f52: split_clauses('search for salt and pepper') -> (['search for salt','pepper'],['and']); split_clauses('tell Sam the demo is at 3 and then we eat') -> 2 clauses. Each clause is a worker().submit_async(self.engine.route, ...) call awaited in a loop (line ~466) before the spec path. Cost = n_clauses x route_ms per rejected utterance (route_ms not measured on M5 here).
fix: Try the whole-utterance route first, reusing the speculative hit. Call _compound only when that route is MULTI_STEP or p_top < tau. Also exclude message-body skills (send_message, compose_email, new_note, type_text) from clause 1 unless the join is 'and then'.

title: BatchCutter skips bare mute/wifi/bluetooth lines; batches exceed 5 actions
detail: The orchestrator calls dsl.action_line(line, catalog.skills), which turns a bare catalog skill line into 'skill <name>' and executes it. BatchCutter calls action_line(line) without skills, so it falls back to the snake_case regex, and catalog skills with no underscore (mute, wifi, bluetooth) are never counted. Those lines run, but the 5-action cap and the keep-the-5th-action's-expect rule (brain-11) do not count them.
evidence: cloud/brain-3 14a3f52: BatchCutter().push over ['mute','wifi on','bluetooth off','mute','wifi off','press #4','keys cmd+s'] leaves n=2, done=False after 7 lines. action_line('mute',{'mute'})='skill mute' but action_line('mute')=None.
fix: Pass the catalog skill set into BatchCutter (BatchCutter(skills=catalog.skills)) and call action_line(line, self.skills).

title: Brain on main ignores new HandsKit fields: web_ax_pending, script exit, no_text_target
detail: AGENTS.md@2a72c34 and HandsKit@894df52 add three observe/act result fields. Main's brain handles none of them. (1) web_ax_pending: Chrome's web AX tree fills about 2 s after a switch. Main plans on the empty first observe, so it acts blind or falls back to screenshots. (2) Shell scripts now fail with exit_code/stderr/timed_out. Main shows a generic 'Script failed' and the planner never sees stderr. (3) type/type_text fail with error 'no_text_target' plus an `observed` hint. The planner batch log carries only the error string, not the hint, and the System 1 reply is 'Couldn't type text. Try saying it differently?', which misleads because the fix is focusing a field. cloud/brain-3 14a3f52 covers (1) and (2), but (3) is unhandled on both branches.
evidence: grep counts at main 280715d orchestrator.py: web_ax_pending=0, exit_code=0, no_text_target=0. At cloud/brain-3: web_ax_pending=3, exit_code=2, no_text_target=0. brain-3 replies.fail_text has no no_text_target branch, so the default reply 'Couldn't {human(name)}...' is used. _rpc_action's failure dict at ~854 keeps res, but the batch _log line uses only the error string.
fix: Merge cloud/brain-3 for (1) and (2), after brain-16 is fixed. For (3): in _rpc_action, when error=='no_text_target' append f" (observed: {res.get('observed')})" to the _log line. In replies.fail_text, map no_text_target to 'Click a text field first, then ask again.'
